# Verdict: ACCEPT-WITH-RESERVATIONS ## Overall Assessment This is a well-constructed modal dialog that implements the WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog pattern with genuine care. The focus trap is recomputed per-keystroke, the backdrop dismissal is guarded against text-selection drags, and the focus save/restore lifecycle is isolated from the Escape handler to survive unstable `onClose` identities. The core ARIA pattern is complete and coherent. One MAJOR edge-case gap (no focus target when the dialog contains zero focusable children) and one MINOR structural issue (hardcoded `id`) prevent a clean ACCEPT. ## Pre-commitment Predictions Before reading the code, I predicted: 1. Focus trap would miss an edge case (e.g., zero focusable elements) — **confirmed** 2. Focus restoration would race with unmount — **not confirmed; cleanup ordering is correct** 3. The `✕` close glyph would be announced as "times" by screen readers — **not confirmed; `aria-label` correctly overrides content** 4. Hardcoded `id="modal-title"` would collide across instances — **confirmed** 5. Missing `inert` on background content — **partially confirmed; `aria-modal` + focus trap cover the APG requirement, `inert` is an enhancement** 6. Missing `prefers-reduced-motion` for the close-button transition — **confirmed (minor)** ## Critical Findings None. No finding blocks access entirely for a user category under normal usage. ## Major Findings ### 1. Focus is never moved into the dialog when it contains zero focusable children **Evidence:** `Modal.jsx` — initial focus block and focus-trap guard: ```jsx // Initial focus (line ~30) const firstFocusable = getFocusableElements(modalRef.current)[0]; firstFocusable?.focus(); // ← no-op when list is empty; focus stays on trigger // Focus trap (line ~62) if (focusableElements.length === 0) { e.preventDefault(); // ← Tab is swallowed; user cannot enter the dialog return; } ``` **User group impacted:** Keyboard-only and screen-reader users. **Why this matters:** An informational modal ("Your order has been placed. A confirmation email is on its way.") with no buttons, links, or inputs is a common pattern. In that case: - Focus remains on the trigger element *behind* the modal. - Tab/Shift+Tab are swallowed by the trap (`preventDefault`), so the user cannot move focus into the dialog. - The only exit is Escape. The user is effectively stranded on the trigger with no way to interact with the dialog content via keyboard. - A screen-reader user hears "dialog" announced but cannot navigate into it with the keyboard; they must fall back to virtual-cursor browsing, which is a degraded experience. Per the WAI-ARIA APG **Modal Dialog** pattern: *"When the dialog is opened, focus must be moved into the dialog."* The current implementation satisfies this only when at least one focusable child exists. **Fix:** 1. Add `tabindex="-1"` to the `.modal-dialog` div so it can receive programmatic focus. 2. In the initial-focus `setTimeout`, fall back to the dialog element: ```jsx const firstFocusable = getFocusableElements(modalRef.current)[0]; (firstFocusable || modalRef.current).focus(); ``` 3. In the focus-trap handler, treat the dialog element itself as a valid focus position. When focus is on the dialog (or outside it) and focusable children exist, move to the first/last child. When no children exist, `preventDefault` keeps focus on the dialog: ```jsx if (!modalRef.current.contains(activeElement) || activeElement === modalRef.current) { e.preventDefault(); if (focusableElements.length > 0) { (e.shiftKey ? lastElement : firstElement).focus(); } return; } ``` - **Confidence:** HIGH - **WCAG / APG:** WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order); WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog — "focus must be moved into the dialog" --- ## Minor Findings ### 2. Hardcoded `id="modal-title"` collides across simultaneous modal instances **Evidence:** `Modal.jsx` — dialog element: ```jsx

{title}

// ← static string ``` **User group impacted:** Screen-reader users (wrong title announced when two modals coexist). **Why this matters:** If a parent renders two `` instances (e.g., a settings modal with a nested confirmation dialog), both `aria-labelledby` attributes resolve to the *first* `#modal-title` in the DOM. The second modal announces the first modal's title. This also breaks if the component is rendered in a mobile/desktop duplicate. **Fix:** Use React 18's `useId()` (or a `useRef`-generated ID) to produce a unique ID per instance: ```jsx const id = useId(); // ... aria-labelledby={id} // ...

{title}

``` - **Confidence:** HIGH - **WCAG / APG:** WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) — the accessible name must resolve to the correct element --- ## Enhancements ### 3. No `inert` attribute on background content `aria-modal="true"` instructs screen readers to ignore background content, and the focus trap handles Tab. However, `aria-modal` does **not** prevent programmatic focus or screen-reader virtual-cursor navigation from reaching background elements. Adding `inert` to the main page wrapper (or using a library like `react-inert`) would provide a more robust guarantee. This is an enhancement, not a gap: the APG Modal Dialog pattern requires focus trapping (implemented) and does not mandate `inert`. - **WCAG:** 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap) — the existing trap satisfies this; `inert` is belt-and-suspenders ### 4. Close-button `transition: color 0.2s` does not respect `prefers-reduced-motion` The only animation in the component is a 0.2 s color transition on `.modal-close:hover`. It is subtle, but a user with vestibular sensitivity who has `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set will still see it. **Fix:** ```css @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .modal-close { transition: none; } } ``` - **WCAG:** 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions) — non-essential animation should be suppressible ### 5. No `role="alertdialog"` option for destructive-action modals The component hardcodes `role="dialog"`. When the modal is used for a destructive confirmation ("Delete this project?"), `role="alertdialog"` is the semantically correct role — it signals urgency to screen readers and is announced differently ("alert dialog" vs. "dialog"). **Fix:** Accept a `role` prop (defaulting to `"dialog"`) so the parent can pass `"alertdialog"` when appropriate: ```jsx const Modal = ({ isOpen, onClose, title, children, role = "dialog" }) => { // ...
``` - **WCAG / APG:** WAI-ARIA APG Modal Dialog — "Use `role="alertdialog"` for dialogs that convey an alert or require immediate user attention" ### 6. `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'` does not cover scrollable ancestors If the modal is rendered inside a scrollable container (e.g., a `
` with `overflow-y: auto`), disabling `body` scroll does not prevent that container from scrolling. A more robust approach is to set `overflow: hidden` on the nearest scrollable ancestor, or use the `overflow-anchor` / `scroll-lock` pattern. This is an enhancement; the common case (body-level scroll) is handled. --- ## What's Missing (Gap Analysis) | Gap | Why it matters | Severity | |-----|---------------|----------| | No `tabindex="-1"` fallback on the dialog element | Read-only modals leave focus stranded on the trigger (see Major #1) | MAJOR | | No unique-ID generation | Multi-modal scenarios break `aria-labelledby` resolution (see Minor #2) | MINOR | | No `inert` on background content | Virtual-cursor / programmatic focus can still reach background | ENHANCEMENT | | No `prefers-reduced-motion` guard | 0.2 s transition plays for vestibular-sensitive users | ENHANCEMENT | | No `role` prop for `alertdialog` | Destructive-action modals lack urgency semantics | ENHANCEMENT | | No `aria-describedby` support | Parent cannot attach supplementary instructions to the dialog | ENHANCEMENT | | No mechanism to move focus to new content when children change dynamically | A form that submits and shows a success message inside the modal won't shift focus to the message | ENHANCEMENT (parent responsibility) | --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes | Perspective | Alarm Level | Assessment | |-------------|-------------|------------| | **Screen reader** | MEDIUM | `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` + `aria-labelledby` are correct. The dialog is announced with its title. The close button is named "Close dialog." The backdrop is `role="presentation"` and invisible to AT. **Gap:** hardcoded ID can cause wrong title announcement in multi-modal scenarios. **Gap:** read-only modals leave focus outside the dialog. | | **Keyboard-only** | HIGH | Tab/Shift+Tab cycle is correct and recomputed per keystroke. Escape closes. Focus restores on close. Focus indicator is visible (2–3 px outline, `#0066cc` on white ≈ 4.5:1+). **Gap:** zero-focusable-child modals strand the user on the trigger with Tab swallowed. | | **Low vision** | LOW | Focus outlines are 2–3 px with adequate contrast. Close button hit area ≈ 32 × 32 px (exceeds 24 × 24 WCAG 2.5.8 minimum). Text colors `#333`/`#666` on white pass 4.5:1. Modal is `max-width: 500px; width: 90%` — reflows at 200% zoom. No sticky-element occlusion. | | **Cognitive** | LOW | Single clear close button with a plain-language label. Escape is a standard, discoverable exit. No timeouts, no multi-step flows, no ambiguous state. Interaction model is consistent with platform conventions. | | **Vestibular & motion** | LOW | One 0.2 s color transition on the close button. No parallax, no auto-playing content, no flashing. `prefers-reduced-motion` not set (see Enhancement #4). | | **Auditory access** | LOW | No audio or video content. No auto-playing sound. | | **Environmental contrast** | LOW | All text/background pairs pass WCAG 1.4.3. No color-only state indicators. Focus indicators meet 2.4.7 and 2.4.13. | --- ## Verdict Justification **ACCEPT-WITH-RESERVATIONS** rather than ACCEPT because: - The MAJOR finding (zero-focusable-child focus gap) is a real accessibility failure for a plausible usage pattern (informational modals). It does not block the common case (modals with at least a close button), but it is a design gap that will surface in user testing or a screen-reader audit. - The MINOR finding (hardcoded ID) is a latent bug that will break in multi-modal or duplicate-render scenarios. Neither finding blocks the core interaction model. The ARIA pattern is complete, the focus trap is well-engineered (recomputed per keystroke, handles dynamic children, recovers stray focus), the backdrop dismissal is correctly guarded, and the focus save/restore lifecycle is properly isolated. The component is in good shape; the two findings above are the reservations. **To upgrade to ACCEPT:** 1. Add `tabindex="-1"` to the dialog and focus it when no focusable children exist (fixes Major #1). 2. Replace the hardcoded `id="modal-title"` with `useId()` (fixes Minor #2). --- ## Open Questions (unscored) 1. **Focus restoration when the trigger is unmounted:** If the parent removes the trigger element from the DOM in the same render that sets `isOpen={false}`, `previouslyFocusedElement.current?.focus()` targets a detached node and silently fails. Focus falls to ``. Is this a scenario your parent components can produce? If so, consider a fallback (e.g., focus the first heading or `
`). 2. **`onClose` called from multiple sources simultaneously:** If both the Escape handler and the backdrop click fire in the same event loop tick (e.g., a user presses Escape while clicking the backdrop), `onClose` is called twice. The parent's `isOpen` state should be idempotent, but is it? If `onClose` triggers a side effect (e.g., an API call), double-invocation could be a problem. 3. **Nested modals:** The component does not document or handle nested modal scenarios (a modal opened from within a modal). The focus trap, Escape handler, and focus restoration are all scoped to a single modal instance. If nesting is a use case, the design needs a modal stack with per-instance focus management. 4. **`getClientRects().length > 0` filter:** This correctly excludes `display: none` elements but does not exclude elements hidden via `clip: rect(0,0,0,0)` or `position: absolute; left: -9999px` (common "visually hidden" patterns). If a modal contains a visually-hidden skip link or off-screen element, it would be included in the focusable list. Is this a concern for your use cases?
